industry.headline: UK consultation moving toward under-16 social media ban by spring 2027
industry.summary: UK government plans to ban under-16s from social media platforms by spring 2027, alongside default protections for 16-17 year-olds including overnight access restrictions (midnight-6am), muted overnight notifications, and autoplay/personalized feeds off by default. Directly impacts NOMO's UK pilot market where CEO Leonardo is already engaging policymakers.

industry.headline: Wisconsin AG Kaul sues TikTok over youth mental health harms
industry.summary: Wisconsin's AG sued TikTok alleging it knowingly deployed addictive features (recommendation engine, infinite scroll, autoplay, push notifications, LIVE) targeting children while deceiving parents, joining a wave of state AG actions following Alabama's $100M settlement and the $16.68B multistate Meta settlement — reinforcing demand for off-social-media alternatives like NOMO.

industry.headline: NetChoice sues New York over social media mental-health warning label law
industry.summary: Tech trade group NetChoice sued to block New York's law requiring an unskippable Surgeon-General-style warning when minors open social apps with addictive feeds, autoplay, or infinite scroll (effective Jan 1). Regardless of outcome, the fight over addictive-design mandates reinforces the narrative NOMO's reward model is built around.

industry.headline: Harvard study: strict phone bans add 1-2 weeks of learning a year
industry.summary: A Harvard economist's research finds school phone bans measurably improve learning outcomes, though researchers want platforms to extend restrictions so students don't just switch apps after hours; cites Meta's $17B settlement requiring overnight app blocks and findings that sleep is the strongest predictor of teen digital wellbeing — direct validation of NOMO's focus/sleep value proposition and the after-school coverage gap NOMO fills.

industry.headline: Teens, in Open Letter, Criticize Adults Over Social Media Bans: 'Do the Real Work'
industry.summary: Teen leaders argue blanket bans dodge the 'real work' of oversight, digital literacy, and safer product design, citing UNICEF data that teens already circumvent bans and that many LGBTQ teens rely on online community for safety — a youth-voice counter-narrative that favors reward-based alternatives like NOMO over prohibition.

industry.headline: Apple adds Social Media-specific 'Time Allowances' and age-rating questions for apps
industry.summary: iOS/iPadOS/macOS 27 add parental 'Time Allowances' to cap time in categories including Social Media, and require developers to disclose social-media capabilities so the new category applies correctly — a platform-level feature that validates NOMO's core premise and could become a complementary or competing enforcement layer for schools and parents.

industry.headline: Italy set to restrict social media access for teenagers by year-end
industry.summary: Italy is preparing a security decree (expected by December) barring under-13s from social media accounts, requiring parental-linked accounts for 13-15 year-olds, and mandating AGCOM age-verification guidance within nine months — part of a fast-expanding EU/global patchwork following UK and Australia that NOMO's CEO is already engaging with on policy.

industry.headline: Loyalty Newswire: new rewards-platform funding, consolidation and market-sizing moves
industry.summary: Recent loyalty-industry moves include Sunoco unifying loyalty programs onto one platform, Points4Purpose expanding US payments/loyalty targeting the $31B loyalty market, and experiential-rewards startup Squeez taking a $1M investment — continued market validation of the gamified/experiential rewards mechanics underpinning NOMO's Moments model.
